blocks.title: External Considerations and Governance Structures comparison
External Considerations and Governance Structures exam shortcuts
items: Requirement comes from a regulator → REGULATORY
The source is a regulatory authority or sector rule.
Example: A financial regulator requires specific controls.
Legal obligations can come from statutes, contracts, or litigation.
Example: Privacy law requires specific handling of personal data.
Head office sets one security policy for all units → CENTRALIZED
Authority is concentrated in one central function.
Example: Corporate security approves all standards.
Regional units make their own security decisions → DECENTRALIZED
Authority is distributed closer to local operations.
Example: Each region adapts controls to local requirements.
Board reviews cybersecurity risk → BOARD GOVERNANCE
Boards provide strategic oversight and accountability.
Example: Board risk committee reviews major cyber risks.
blocks.example: First decide whether the scenario is about policy direction, a technical requirement, a step-by-step process, external obligations, or ownership/accountability.

questions.q: A financial institution changes controls because its sector regulator issued a new requirement. Which external consideration is this?
questions.explanation: Regulatory considerations come from regulatory authorities or sector rules.

questions.q: A company must change its privacy practices because a new law takes effect. Which consideration is most direct?
questions.explanation: Legal considerations arise from laws, contracts, or other legal obligations.

questions.q: A security framework is adopted because it is widely expected in the company's industry, even though it is not required by law. Which consideration is this?
questions.explanation: Industry considerations arise from sector norms and expectations.

questions.q: Corporate security sets one policy that all business units must follow. Which governance model is this?
questions.explanation: Centralized governance concentrates authority in a central team.

questions.q: Each regional business unit is allowed to make its own security-control decisions. Which governance model is this?
A board risk committee reviews major cybersecurity risks and holds executives accountable. What governance structure is this?
questions.explanation: Boards provide strategic oversight and accountability.

questions.q: A cross-functional security steering group reviews policy changes and risk issues. What type of governance structure is this?
questions.explanation: Committees coordinate and make decisions for a specific governance area.
